Plot a scatterplot of two variables, split by a group

Source: R/plotscat.R
plotscat_split.Rd

This is called by plotscat() when z is a grouping variable. It plots x against y for the first two levels of z, and tests whether the correlations differ (cocor, Fisher 1925).

Usage

plotscat_split(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  z,
  cl = 2,
  condcols = NULL,
  results_title = TRUE,
  title_text = NULL,
  outp = "",
  bayes_factor = F
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per participant.

x

Name of the x column.

y

Name of the y column.

z

Name of the column splitting the groups.

cl

2 plots a line for each sub group, 1 plots just the main line.

condcols

Colours for the groups. By default they are chosen by replacecondcols().

results_title

Show the statistics in the plot title?

title_text

Optional text for the title.

outp

Not used.

bayes_factor

Calculate the Bayes factor for the difference between groups?

Value

A list with the plot (p) and the statistics. The results for the first and second group are sigyz1.* and sigyz2.*.
